project.title: Cognitive Bias Ontology
project.introText: An ontology for a cluster of cognitive biases, part of a collective ontology of human biases built by the whole class of Knowledge Representation and Extraction (prof. Aldo Gangemi, University of Bologna, 2022/23).

gridImages.caption: The Illusory Correlation ontology drawn from its OWL file: the “Lucky Charm Socks” user story as individuals linked by object properties, coloured by whether each class comes from Framester, a design pattern, DBpedia or the team.
Reuse matrix: which content ontology design patterns and Framester frames each of the 16 ontologies uses in its story graph (filled) or only names in its documentation (outlined).
Properties the group reused across user stories, led by exob:isEngagedIn from the Experience & Observation pattern in 12 of the 16 ontologies.

project.middleText: Our group, Marco Lamorte, Corrado Consiglio, Salvatore Di Marzo and I, modelled sixteen biases, from the gambler's fallacy and the hot hand fallacy to pareidolia, naive realism and the blind spot bias. Each went through the same eXtreme Design workflow: research and documentation, ideation and design, modelling and implementation, then presentation and visualisation. ChatGPT and Gemini were used early on for definitions, scenarios and user stories, and Framester among the resources for modelling.
project.conclusionText: The process is documented in a public GitBook. It showed how much understanding of a domain an ontology needs before any modelling starts, and where language models help and where their answers had to be corrected. The 2026 explorer draws each user story as a graph of the individuals in its OWL file, maps which design patterns and Framester frames each ontology reuses, and shows the vocabulary the group shared.

project.reworkNote: The ontologies were built as a group project with Marco Lamorte, Corrado Consiglio and Salvatore Di Marzo for Knowledge Representation and Extraction (2022/23). In 2026 I independently built a visual explorer from the group's OWL files and documentation; the images here come from it, and it is not yet published.
